abstract: We show that fluctuations in the ratio of noncore to core funding in the banking systems of advanced economies are largely driven by three global factors of both real and financial natures, with country‐specific factors playing only a minor role. Exchange rate flexibility helps insulate the noncore to core ratio from such global factors. This insulation is stronger in periods away from global crises. Tighter prudential regulations appear to have a complementary effect to exchange rate insulation.
abstract_zh: 我们证明，发达经济体银行体系中非核心融资与核心融资之比的波动，主要由三个兼具实体与金融性质的全球因素驱动，而国别特定因素的作用甚微。汇率灵活性有助于使非核心与核心之比免受此类全球因素的影响。在全球危机之外的时期，这种隔离效应更为显著。更严格的审慎监管似乎对汇率隔离具有补充作用。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Global Factors in Noncore Bank Funding and Exchange Rate Flexibility
title_zh: 非核心银行融资中的全球因素与汇率弹性

abstract: Changes to regulatory environments influence firm-level incentives, which can move the productivity frontier or reposition firms within an existing frontier. Estimating causal effects of policy changes requires a credible counterfactual for productivity in the absence of policy change. We estimate causal effects of a major policy change in agricultural markets; deregulation of the Canadian Wheat Board. The Canadian Wheat Board was a state-trading enterprise that controlled sale and distribution of wheat and barley produced in Western Canada through a single-desk monopsony from 1943 to 2012. We investigate how deregulation affected farm-level productivity for regulated crops. Field-level production and input data for 13,000 farms over 17 years are used to generate a within-farm difference-in-differences estimate of how relative productivity changed between regulated and unregulated crops when the single-desk mandate was removed. Our within-farm approach identifies the effects of regime change while controlling for factors that confound productivity estimation in other approaches, including unobserved time-varying factors at the farm level. We identify significant positive effects of deregulation on farm-level productivity of spring wheat. We also find heterogeneous effects across fields with different land productivity, and across farms with different levels of experience marketing their unregulated crops outside the single-desk. Broadly, we find that deregulation of the Canadian Wheat Board's monopsonistic single desk incentivized farms to increase productivity of wheat. This research contributes to the understanding of how policy interventions can affect firm-level productivity, and to the productivity literature with an estimation strategy for identifying productivity effects in the context of multi-output firms.
abstract_zh: 监管环境的变化会影响企业层面的激励，从而可能推动生产率前沿的移动或使企业在现有前沿内重新定位。评估政策变化的因果效应需要一个在没有政策变化情况下生产率的可信反事实。我们评估了农业市场一项重大政策变化的因果效应——加拿大小麦委员会放松管制。加拿大小麦委员会是一个国有贸易企业，从1943年到2012年通过单一垄断渠道控制着加拿大西部生产的小麦和大麦的销售与分配。我们研究了放松管制如何影响受监管作物的农场层面生产率。利用17年间13,000个农场的田间层面生产和投入数据，我们生成了农场内部双重差分估计，以衡量在单一垄断授权被取消后，受监管与未受监管作物之间相对生产率的变化。我们的农场内部方法在控制其他方法中混淆生产率估计的因素（包括农场层面未观测到的时变因素）的同时，识别了制度变化的影响。我们发现放松管制对春小麦农场层面生产率产生了显著的正向效应。我们还发现，在不同土地生产率的田块之间，以及在不同水平经验在单一垄断之外销售其未受监管作物的农场之间，存在异质性效应。总体而言，我们发现加拿大小麦委员会垄断性单一渠道的放松管制激励了农场提高小麦生产率。这项研究有助于理解政策干预如何影响企业层面生产率，并为多产出企业背景下识别生产率效应的估计策略贡献于生产率文献。
title: Market regulation and productivity: The case of the Canadian Wheat Board
title_zh: 市场规制与生产率：以加拿大小麦局为例
